source.title: Where Grokking Happens: Distributed Utility and Fourier Recoding Without a Module Switch

record.tranche_reason: The study trains small algorithmic Transformers and observes delayed generalization, but uses exact activation-allocation, probe, removal, and path-restoration analyses to test the transition mechanism rather than reproducing the original measurement alone.
record.gate_note: The study reports grokking behavior in the main addition runs and tests several proposed transition mechanisms. It does not compare training-set sizes to test whether smaller sets require more optimization. The prime-by-width-by-head factorial and optimizer analyses are not direct tests of the listed non-algorithmic, weight-norm, large-model, or numerical-artifact versions.
record.test_reason: Trains small Transformers on modular arithmetic and reports delayed generalization. It then tests what changes across the transition with paired exact activation games, Fourier Owen allocations, probes and selective removal. This is a different method aimed at the original mechanism question. The study is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. In these small Transformers, grokking is spectral recoding of an existing distributed circuit, not a module switch. Attention leads already at memorization, reversing the MLP-to-attention handoff prediction. Selected block-0 Fourier modes become OOD-useful, and their effect flows chiefly through the final MLP. Nonzero residuals, metric-sensitive boundaries and a failed cross-prime ridge rule out a unique instruction or universal architecture law.
record.recipe_differences: Uses small algorithmic modular arithmetic and trains small Transformers to delayed generalization, but the main contribution is a different measurement/intervention recipe: paired exact activation-replacement games, Fourier subspace Owen allocations, probes, selective removals, and path restoration. The study does not perform the training-set-size sweep needed to test the delay-versus-data-size part of V1.
record.method_sensitivity: Results are reported under mean, zero, and same-split donor replacements and under clipped compression, unclipped log-likelihood advantage, and accuracy allocation. The paper reports metric sensitivity for division and the factorial tests; donor replacement preserves the central block-0 and selected-mode directions. Training-set size is not swept for delay.

fits_no_version.finding: Transition gain is distributed across embedding, attention and MLP, with a relative block-0 attention excess confirmed in fresh addition and division cohorts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking is not a winner-take-all module switch; all residual paths gain OOD utility.

fits_no_version.finding: The MLP-memorizes/attention-generalizes handoff reverses: MLP-minus-attention training utility is −.3314 at the memory anchor (0/12 in the predicted direction).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorization is not localized in MLPs ahead of an attention-based generalizing phase.

fits_no_version.finding: The selected-mode effect is mediated mainly through block-1 MLP (2.6440 vs .1273 for the other paths).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The Fourier recoding in early attention is read out chiefly through the final MLP.

fits_no_version.finding: The cross-prime head-dimension ridge holds at p=43 (.2115) but not p=53 (.0191); routing is saturated before generalization and participation ratios do not collapse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architectural moderators of the grokking mechanism are prime-specific; no rank collapse accompanies grokking.

record.problems: Evidence is from small tied-embedding Transformers and synthetic arithmetic tasks. Mechanism cohorts generally contain 11–12 pairs; the authors note five-hundred-step sampling limits timing precision. The strict-anchor audit corrected 8/12 earlier p47 checkpoints. Activation replacement creates hybrid counterfactuals, donor replacement preserves marginals rather than joint dependence, and the study does not test the dataset-size delay relationship. The study itself identifies metric-sensitive boundaries and a failed cross-prime ridge.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional transfer, utility-sensitivity, Fourier-selection, residual-decomposition, factorial, head, routing, participation-ratio, and path-discovery results. They were not included because they do not add a distinct direct test of V1/V2 beyond the retained rows, or are exploratory/secondary checks. In particular, the base path-discovery MLP0-versus-direct comparison was null (−.0224; 4/12; §4.5, Appendix I), but the disjoint block-1 MLP confirmation is retained in r21.

untested.parts: No training-set-size sweep with delays; whether delay grows as the training set shrinks is untested.
Removal or cleanup of memorizing components is not measured. Whether progress measures precede the behavioural jump is not established.
Entire version: no non-algorithmic data, no initialization-scale or weight-norm sweep.
Entire version: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Critical dataset size, ungrokking, and the circuit-efficiency comparison are untested. Only a WD=0 control exists.

No test of whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm. Largest-head identity is unstable and architecture effects are prime-specific, but none of this is framed as an algorithm-identity test.
The β2 manipulation failed its Slingshot manipulation check, and no floating-point/softmax control was run. Whether the delay vanishes under controls is untested.

missing.what: Equal-data WD=0 controls: 12/12 memory-only at the paired generalization step, none transitioned.
Behaviour gates of fresh cohorts: addition 12/12, division 11/12, factorial 95/96 main vs 0/96 controls; p59-v1 7/12.
Division pilot pass counts by training pairs per label: 14, 18, 23 pairs gave 0/3, 3/3, 1/3 (non-monotonic; no delays).
β2=.90 arm: 7/12 transitioned vs 12/12 at .98; spike severity not separated (p=.448); the manipulation failed to suppress Slingshot.
Division pure ratio-mode Owen gain .0219 (7/11) vs same-frequency context .2836 (11/11).
Median transition delay by prime at matched density: 3,800 vs 2,275 steps.

record.verdict_notes: Most localization rows (r3–r7, r18–r21) answer 'where', which no version names, so they move to fits_no_version. V2 support comes from the Fourier recoding rows. 'Anticipation' is only weakly addressed because the transition interval is bounded by OOD accuracy itself. The V5 label rests on text from Appendix K, not a row. Optimizer results cannot test V7 because the manipulation check failed.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not sweep training-set size to test whether a smaller training set increases the optimization delay.

The study measures activation-game utility, decoding, selected-mode removal, and path mediation; it does not establish a literal parameter-level circuit or measure memorizing components being removed as generalization begins.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or lazy-to-rich transition test.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
No test of a low-norm efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking below such a size.
The study does not establish that runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm across architectures and hyperparameters.
The optimizer analysis does not test whether grokking delays disappear after controlling adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point softmax limits.

rows.subject: Base p47 addition runs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Train on the restricted modular-addition dataset and evaluate train and OOD accuracy every 50 steps.
rows.measure: Memory-first and persistent-generalization criteria; delay between them
rows.value: 12/12 runs passed both criteria; median delay was 3,725 steps. Memory required train accuracy ≥ .99 and OOD accuracy ≤ .35; persistent generalization required train ≥ .99 and OOD ≥ .90 at three consecutive evaluations, at least 1,000 steps later.
rows.note: The study reports that all main runs first reached the memory-dominant state and later met the persistent-generalization criterion.

rows.subject: Nested low-data addition controls (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Train matched controls on the first five pairs per label from the same seeded permutation.
rows.note: This is a low-data control comparison, not a sweep that tests delay as a function of training-set size.
rows.check: 0/12 five-pair controls generalized within 30,000 steps. This cannot separate a longer delay from no grokking, and no delay is measured, so 'absent' is the wrong state for V1's delay-vs-size clause. Treat it as a control.
